inspiration.observed_pattern: A common table expression self-joins dated records with an ordered identifier pair and inclusive start/end predicates to find overlapping intervals.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as an independently authored shift-conflict report. Shifts are paired only within the same team, the inclusive boundary rule retains a zero-minute handoff, and CASE plus TIMESTAMPDIFF classifies ordinary overlaps versus touching shifts. The table, rows, labels, and scheduling purpose are new.

fixture_notes: Shifts 1 and 2 overlap for 30 minutes, shifts 2 and 3 touch at an inclusive endpoint, shift 2 and shift 6 overlap for 30 minutes, and the different-team shift must not pair.
determinism_notes: All timestamps and team labels are fixed, each pair is ordered by the unique shift IDs, and the report uses no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections.
setup: CREATE TABLE team_shifts (shift_id INT PRIMARY KEY, team_code VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL, starts_at DATETIME NOT NULL, ends_at DATETIME NOT NULL)

steps.sql: WITH overlap_pairs AS (SELECT first_shift.shift_id AS first_shift_id, second_shift.shift_id AS second_shift_id, CASE WHEN first_shift.ends_at = second_shift.starts_at OR second_shift.ends_at = first_shift.starts_at THEN 'touching' ELSE 'overlapping' END AS relation, TIMESTAMPDIFF(MINUTE, CASE WHEN first_shift.starts_at > second_shift.starts_at THEN first_shift.starts_at ELSE second_shift.starts_at END, CASE WHEN first_shift.ends_at < second_shift.ends_at THEN first_shift.ends_at ELSE second_shift.ends_at END) AS overlap_minutes FROM team_shifts first_shift JOIN team_shifts second_shift ON first_shift.team_code = second_shift.team_code AND first_shift.shift_id < second_shift.shift_id AND first_shift.ends_at >= second_shift.starts_at AND first_shift.starts_at <= second_shift.ends_at) SELECT first_shift_id, second_shift_id, relation, overlap_minutes FROM overlap_pairs ORDER BY first_shift_id, second_shift_id
